description:
memory.rs:149-158 (objects_mut) and 178-181 (aux_mut). Both helpers exist to "return a &mut to the storage HashMap for (type_name, account_id)" — but as a side effect they also call self.known_accounts.insert(account_id.to_owned()), registering the account.

Reading from the call site:

    let map = inner.objects_mut("ContactCard", account_id.as_ref());  // also registers account!

A reader who knows the helper name does not see the registration. account_exists later observes the registration as a fact about the world — which means create_object on a brand-new account quietly creates the account too. That is probably the intent, but the intent is encoded in the side effect of a "mutable accessor".

This is idiomatically wrong for two reasons:
1. The principle of least astonishment: an _mut accessor in idiomatic Rust returns a borrow; it does not perform unrelated state mutations on a separate field of the same struct.
2. The side effect is invisible at call sites. A future refactor that switches from objects_mut to objects_ref (or vice versa) silently changes account-registration semantics.

Idiomatic restructure: separate the two operations.

    pub fn ensure_account(&mut self, account_id: &str) { ... }
    pub fn objects_mut(...) -> &mut HashMap<...> { ... } // pure accessor

Call sites then read:

    inner.ensure_account(account_id);
    let map = inner.objects_mut("ContactCard", account_id);

…which is honest about what is being mutated.

Same pattern in canonical jmap-mail-server/src/memory.rs:147-151 — propagation needed.
title: Inner::objects_mut and aux_mut silently mutate known_accounts as a side effect
